correctness.rationale: For every nontrivial positive boundary-law solution at \(q=3\) and \(k=4\), taking \(t=z^{1/4}\) is reversible and yields an exact rational parameterization. The transition matrix has exactly the two stated nontrivial eigenvalues. Their ordering follows from a one-factor sign identity. On \(t>1\), \(\lambda_b<1/2\) follows from a shifted polynomial with all positive coefficients. On \(0<t<1\), \(\lambda_a>1/2\) is exactly the sign of the strictly increasing cubic \(t^3+t^2+t-1\), and \(	heta(t)\) is strictly decreasing, giving the exact temperature threshold. The proof distinguishes the strict Kesten–Stigum criterion from its failure and makes no converse claim.

value.rationale: The 2021 survey explicitly identifies \(k\ge4\) as the unconsidered next regime for three-state Potts extremality because nontrivial branch formulas were unavailable. Order four is therefore the first natural finite cutoff after the studied \(k=3\) case. The finding closes the Kesten–Stigum classification for all nontrivial order-four branches and supplies a reusable root-parameter mechanism, rather than an arbitrary numerical slice or a small computational improvement.
